title: Drift check and reconciliation
trigger: Nightly plan of every layer against the code on main
summary: Nightly drift check found one setting in the local environment that differs from the code on main. Applying this work item changes the retention setting for one config map from 1 day to 7 days.

explanation.sentence: Nightly drift check found one setting in the local environment that differs from the code on main. Applying this work item changes the retention setting for one config map from 1 day to 7 days.
explanation.why: The nightly plan of every layer compared live infrastructure with the code on main. The retention setting for the config map kubernetes_config_map_v1.retention is 1 day in the environment, but the code says 7 days. This work item brings the environment back in line with the code.
explanation.downtime: The plan does not replace or destroy anything. It is an in-place update of one config map, so the plan shows no downtime.
explanation.user_effect: No user-visible effect is listed in the plan. The only change is the retention value stored in the config map, which goes from 1 day to 7 days.
explanation.cost_change: The plan does not show any cost change.
explanation.duration: The plan does not state how long the apply takes.
pre_checks: The plans for all three layers are current and none is superseded.
The plan for 30-data changes one resource (kubernetes_config_map_v1.retention) with no adds, destroys, or replaces.
The policy tier is T2 (normal-change). The change does not affect a stateful resource or an identity.
The plans for 40-platform and 50-app show no changes, so they add no risk to this work item.
explanation.backup: The plan does not include a backup step. The change only updates one config map value and does not touch stateful resources.
explanation.rollback: Set the retention value back to 1 day in the code and run the apply again. The plan's policy tier is T2 (normal-change), so the rollback follows the same approval path.
explanation.verification: After the apply, the next nightly plan should show no changes in layer 30-data, and layers 40-platform and 50-app already show no changes.
explanation.if_deferred: No layers are deferred. All three layers (30-data, 40-platform, 50-app) are covered by this approval. Only 30-data has a change. 40-platform and 50-app have no changes.

title: Bump postgres_version to 17.12 in local 30-data (PG-17.12)
trigger: Advisory PG-17.12: Postgres minor release 17.12 is pending; this environment runs 17.11
summary: Upgrade the local Postgres 17 database from 17.11 to 17.12, a minor patch, to apply the pending advisory PG-17.12.

explanation.sentence: Upgrade the local Postgres 17 database from 17.11 to 17.12, a minor patch, to apply the pending advisory PG-17.12.
explanation.why: Advisory PG-17.12 says Postgres 17.12 is released and this local environment still runs 17.11. The change moves the local database to the patched minor version in the 30-data layer (work item WI-0007).
explanation.downtime: The plan does not state a downtime figure. The database StatefulSet image changes, so its pod will restart. Expect the local database to be briefly unavailable during the rollout.
explanation.user_effect: No release note was provided, so the user-visible effect is not documented. The change is a minor patch within Postgres 17, so no schema or application change is expected from the plan itself.
explanation.cost_change: The plan contains no cost data. It creates no resources and changes two existing ones: the database StatefulSet image and the prepare_shared job. It destroys nothing.
explanation.duration: The plan does not give a duration. The work is one image change applied to a local environment, followed by a pod restart.
pre_checks: Confirm a recent backup or snapshot of the local Postgres data exists.
Confirm nothing depends on the local database being available during the pod restart.
Note that prepare_shared is a Kubernetes job that is replaced, so it will run again when applied.
Note that the plan's policy reason says no changed resource is stateful, but the postgres StatefulSet is a stateful workload. Confirm the T2 tier is correct for this change before approving.
explanation.backup: The plan does not describe a backup step. Confirm that a current backup or snapshot of the local database exists before approving, because the plan does not create one.
explanation.rollback: The plan does not describe a rollback procedure. The practical rollback is to set the image back to postgres:17.11-alpine in 30-data and apply again. This is a minor-version change within the same major version, so the data files should remain usable, but the plan does not state this.
explanation.verification: The layer outputs postgres_version. Check that this output reads 17.12 after apply, and that the StatefulSet pod is running the new image.
explanation.if_deferred: Nothing is deferred. The deferred_layers list is empty, so this approval covers only the 30-data layer.

explanation.why: Paperboat 1.2.0-bad is published and local runs 1.1.1. The release makes the inventory list faster by building it from a snapshot for each tank. The image tag contains the word "bad", so confirm that this is the build you intend to run before you approve.
explanation.downtime: The plan does not state any downtime, and the release note does not describe any. The change is a single Helm update of the app, so expect a rolling restart of the app pods.
explanation.user_effect: The inventory board and the rental form load from the new code path. The output stays the same: same fields in the same order. Rentals, deliveries, support, worker jobs, the inventory stream, and the pages themselves do not change.
explanation.cost_change: The plan does not add or change any resources that carry a cost. The base image is the same as 1.1.1.
explanation.duration: The plan does not state a duration. It changes one Helm release.
pre_checks: Confirm that the image tag 1.2.0-bad is the build you intend to deploy, since the name suggests it may be faulty.
Record the current error rate of GET /api/inventory and the errors value in /api/stats so you can compare after the rollout.
Confirm that 1.1.1 is still available so you can roll back.
Confirm that the pre-upgrade hook applies no changes, as the release note states.
explanation.backup: The release note says there is no migration and the schema stays at version 2. The plan does not change stored data, so no data backup is needed for this change. The plan does not state a backup step.
explanation.rollback: Roll back to 1.1.1. The release note says rollback needs no schema change.
explanation.verification: The health check /api/healthz does not call the inventory code, so it will not show a problem in the new path. Watch the error rate of GET /api/inventory and the errors value in /api/stats during and after the rollout. Check the inventory board and the rental form load correctly.

title: Upgrade Paperboat to 1.1.1 (advisory PB-2026-014)
trigger: Advisory PB-2026-014: vulnerability in the base image of Paperboat 1.1.0; fixed in 1.1.1
summary: Upgrade Paperboat from 1.1.0 to 1.1.1 in the local environment to fix advisory PB-2026-014, a vulnerability in the 1.1.0 base image.

explanation.sentence: Upgrade Paperboat from 1.1.0 to 1.1.1 in the local environment to fix advisory PB-2026-014, a vulnerability in the 1.1.0 base image.
explanation.why: Advisory PB-2026-014 reports a vulnerability in the Debian 12 base image of Paperboat 1.1.0. Version 1.1.1 moves to a Debian 13 base image that has the fixed package. The application code does not change. The release note says Paperboat does not call the affected package, so there is no known exploit path through the application. The patch also removes the finding from image scans.
explanation.downtime: The update is a rolling update, so each pod is replaced in turn. Open inventory streams reconnect on their own. The plan does not state a total outage window. Fault injection set through /api/admin/fault is held in memory, so the restart clears it.
explanation.user_effect: No functional change. Users should see the same behavior. Open inventory streams may reconnect once. The version shown in GET /api/version and the UI footer changes to the new base image.
explanation.cost_change: The plan changes only the image tag of one Helm release. It shows no change to any cost-bearing resource.
explanation.duration: The plan does not state a duration. The change is one Helm release update.
pre_checks: Confirm the running version is 1.1.0 before the change.
Confirm the plan is current. It is not superseded.
Confirm the change is in the local environment only, as the plan states.
Confirm no fault injection is needed to stay active after the restart, because the restart clears it.
explanation.backup: No backup step is in this plan. The schema stays at version 2 and the pre-upgrade hook applies nothing, so no data is migrated.
explanation.rollback: Redeploy Paperboat 1.1.0. No schema change is needed. Rolling back restores the vulnerable Debian 12 base image, so the advisory stays open until the patch is applied again.
explanation.verification: Check that GET /api/version reports the new base_image and that the UI footer shows it too. The plan outputs paperboat_version and release_revision, which should show 1.1.1 and the new revision.
explanation.if_deferred: No layers are deferred. This approval covers only layer 50-app.

title: Upgrade Paperboat to 1.1.0 in local
trigger: Paperboat 1.1.0 is published; local runs 1.0.0
summary: Upgrade Paperboat from 1.0.0 to 1.1.0 in the local environment. The plan changes one Helm release and nothing else.

explanation.sentence: Upgrade Paperboat from 1.0.0 to 1.1.0 in the local environment. The plan changes one Helm release and nothing else.
explanation.why: Release 1.1.0 adds fish aging. Each fish gets a condition score, and fish past the retirement age of their species leave the rentable stock.
explanation.downtime: No downtime is expected. The 1.0.0 pods keep serving during the migration and the rolling update.
explanation.user_effect: Each fish shows a condition meter on the inventory board. The board counts retired fish. Health certificates show the condition score. GET /api/inventory adds condition and retire_after_days to each fish. Some fish will change to retired in the first minute after the upgrade, so the number of available fish goes down.
explanation.cost_change: The plan does not state any cost change. It changes only the image tag of one Helm release.
explanation.duration: The plan does not state a duration. The migration runs as a Helm pre-upgrade hook in one transaction, and then the rolling update runs.
pre_checks: Confirm that the plan is the current plan for WI-0002 and is not superseded.
Confirm that the target is the local environment.
Expect the available fish count to drop by the number of fish that retire on the first aging run.
Accept that retirements cannot be undone by a rollback.
explanation.backup: The plan does not include a backup step. The migration only adds columns, but it has no down migration, so a rollback does not remove the new columns.
explanation.rollback: Roll back the Helm release to 1.0.0. No schema change is needed, because 1.0.0 does not read the new columns. Fish that were retired stay retired, and a rollback does not undo retirements.
explanation.verification: After rollout, check fish_available in /api/stats and the aging lines in the worker log. The worker runs the aging job every 30 seconds.
explanation.if_deferred: No layers are deferred under this approval.
